verdict.rationale: GitLab's own docs cover installing, configuring, updating and maintaining a self-managed instance, with several install paths: the Linux package, official Docker images, Helm chart/Operator, and self-compiling. They also give recommended scaling configurations and instance-level controls for GitLab Self-Managed, and community users confirm running private and VM-hosted instances. A community report of backup regressions in 8.15/8.16 is a historical bug, not a contradiction of the capability. Missing for 10: detailed evidence of the upgrade and maintenance procedures beyond a one-line docs mention, plus independent confirmation that recent upgrades go smoothly.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can install, configure, upgrade, and maintain my own instance on my infrastructure

citations.quote: Learn how to install, configure, update, and maintain your GitLab instance.
The Linux package includes services and tools to install GitLab without laborious configuration.
GitLab maintains a set of official Docker images based on the Linux package.
we recommend the Helm chart or the Operator for installing cloud-native GitLab
If the Linux package isn't available for your distribution, you can self-compile GitLab.
Scale your GitLab installation by using the recommended configurations.
A user has run GitLab self-hosted in a VM using the TurnKey Linux GitLab appliance "since forever."
